# Claude Code plugin marketplace (marketplace.json, versions, release tags, team settings) (capability)

<!-- Generated by `stackfoundry pack render` from a researched pack. Each rule cites [key] = a source below.
     Disagree with a rule? Record the repo's way in the pack's repoConvention and re-render, so a refresh keeps
     your decision. -->

Applies to: plugin. Versions in use: 2.1.307 (.github/workflows/ci.yml (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.307, job validate)); 0.1.0 (plugins/stackfoundry/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (version; release tag stackfoundry--v<version>)).

## Rules

- **Change plugin.json `version` in every release meant to reach users, and only there.** Installed copies are cached by computed version: if new commits are pushed without changing `version`, users stay on their cached copy and never receive them (auto-update and `claude plugin update` both compare versions). Here: plugins/stackfoundry/.claude-plugin/plugin.json version; docs/release.md steps 1-2. [host, deps]
- **Do not set `version` on the marketplace entry; keep it in plugin.json alone.** When both are set, plugin.json wins silently at install, and `claude plugin validate` warns `Entry declares version ... but plugin.json says ...`, which fails CI under `--strict`. A second copy also drifts from the tag. Here: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json plugins[stackfoundry] (no version today); tests/test_manifests.py ManifestTests.test_marketplace_entry_does_not_pin_a_conflicting_version. [host, ref]
  This repo: The test tolerates an entry version equal to plugin.json; the docs say not to set it in both places at all.
- **Create release tags with `claude plugin tag plugins/stackfoundry` (dry-run first), never by hand, and never force-move or reuse a `stackfoundry--v<version>` tag.** Dependency ranges resolve against `<plugin>--v<version>` tags and constraint checks use the tag's version, not plugin.json. `claude plugin tag` validates the plugin, checks plugin.json and the marketplace entry agree, requires a clean tree and refuses an existing tag; a hand-made or force-moved tag can name a version whose content differs, and the next install fetches the moved commit. Here: docs/release.md step 4. [deps, cli]
- **Never change the marketplace `name` or the plugin `name`; change the visible label with `displayName`. If a plugin name must change or an entry is removed, add an append-only top-level `renames` map (old -> new or null).** `stackfoundry@stackfoundry` is the install id and the key in users' `enabledPlugins`, `pluginConfigs` and `extraKnownMarketplaces`; a rename breaks every existing install with `Plugin "<name>" not found in marketplace`. Editing an old `renames` entry instead of appending breaks the chain Claude Code follows from the oldest name. Here: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json name, plugins[].name; plugins/stackfoundry/.claude-plugin/plugin.json name; plugins/stackfoundry/skills/init/SKILL.md settings.json row (extraKnownMarketplaces.stackfoundry, enabledPlugins["stackfoundry@stackfoundry"]); README.md install lines; plugins/stackfoundry/README.md install lines. [host, ref]
- **Keep the marketplace entry `name` identical to plugin.json `name`.** The entry name is the install id; the manifest name is the skill prefix. When they differ, installing by the manifest name fails with `Plugin "<manifest-name>" not found in marketplace`. Here: tests/test_manifests.py ManifestTests.test_marketplace_lists_the_plugin_by_its_own_name. [create]
- **Write a relative `source` from the marketplace root with a leading `./`, forward slashes and no `..`, and distribute the marketplace as a git repository (`owner/repo`), never as a bare marketplace.json URL.** A path with `..` or without `./` fails validation; a path to a missing directory passes validation and fails only at install (`Source path does not exist`). A URL-added marketplace downloads only marketplace.json, so every relative-path entry fails at install. Here: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json plugins[stackfoundry].source "./plugins/stackfoundry". [create, ref, host]
- **Validate with `--strict` on both the marketplace root and the plugin directory, at a pinned CLI version.** Claude Code ignores unknown keys at load time, so a typo in a field loads silently; only `--strict` turns the `Unknown field` warning into a failure. A marketplace-root run does not open the skill, agent, command or hook files of the listed plugin, so the plugin needs its own run. Here: .github/workflows/ci.yml job validate. [ref, cli]
- **Key the project-scope `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry by the marketplace `name` (`stackfoundry`) with a `github` source, and pair it with `enabledPlugins["stackfoundry@stackfoundry"]`; skip both in the marketplace repo itself.** Repository `extraKnownMarketplaces` applies only after the contributor accepts the folder trust dialog and is ignored without a message in an untrusted folder (and in `-p` runs unless trust was accepted before); a key that differs from the marketplace name registers nothing usable. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/init/SKILL.md section 4, settings.json row and 'A repo that is itself the stackfoundry marketplace'. [org, ref]
- **Do not add `strict`, component fields, `headers`/`headersHelper` or `dependencies` to the marketplace entry; declare components in the plugin directory.** With `strict: false` an entry that declares components makes the plugin fail to load (`conflicting manifests`); entry `hooks` written as a path pass validation and never run; `headers` on a non-archive source have no effect. Here: not used here yet. [ref]

## Bug categories

| Category | Look for | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| `unreleased-change` (confirm) | A diff that changes files under plugins/stackfoundry/ for users without changing plugin.json `version` (and the CHANGELOG section) before tagging. | Users on the cached version never receive the change; auto-update sees nothing new. [host] |
| `identifier-rename` (blocker) | Any edit to marketplace.json `name`, a plugins[].name, or plugin.json `name`, or removal of an entry, without a matching `renames` entry. | Every existing install and every repo's enabledPlugins/extraKnownMarketplaces key stops resolving (`not found in marketplace`). [host] |
| `version-drift` (confirm) | A version on the marketplace entry, a tag created with plain `git tag`, or a tag whose version differs from plugin.json at the tagged commit. | plugin.json silently wins over the entry; dependents resolve a tag whose content does not match its version. [host, deps] |
| `unresolvable-source` (blocker) | A relative `source` without `./`, with `..`, with backslashes, or pointing at a directory that does not exist; instructions that add the marketplace by a raw marketplace.json URL. | Validation may pass (missing directory) while every install fails with `Source path does not exist` or a path-outside-marketplace error. [create, ref, host] |
| `silently-ignored-field` (suggestion) | A misspelled or unsupported key in marketplace.json or the entry (e.g. a field meant for plugin.json, entry `hooks` as a path). | Claude Code ignores it at load, so the intended behaviour never happens; only `validate --strict` or a load error reveals it. [ref] |

## Testing

Unit tests prove the two manifests agree (names, source path, semver, no conflicting version); `claude plugin validate --strict` proves the schema; `claude plugin tag --dry-run` proves tag/version agreement before a release; only an install from the pushed marketplace proves the source resolves.

- Harness: tests/test_manifests.py ManifestTests; .github/workflows/ci.yml job validate
- Run: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; `claude plugin validate --strict .`; `claude plugin validate --strict plugins/stackfoundry`; `claude plugin tag plugins/stackfoundry --dry-run`
- Trap: A relative source pointing at a missing directory passes validate; assert the path exists and stays inside the root (the test resolves it but does not check `./` prefix or absence of `..`).
- Trap: Validating the marketplace root does not open the plugin's component files; keep the separate plugin run.
- Trap: Local edits from a marketplace added by local path load in place without a version bump, so a local test cannot show that users would miss an unbumped release.
- Sources: [create, ref, cli]

## Security

- A plugin runs hooks and its bin/ executables with the user's full privileges, outside the sandbox, and auto-update replaces reviewed files without re-approval. Treat any release diff touching hooks/hooks.json, bin/ or scripts/ as security-relevant for every installed user. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json; plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh. [security]
- Marketplace names that imitate official Anthropic names, contain non-ASCII characters, or match reserved names are refused, and an already-registered one stops loading with its plugins. `stackfoundry` is not reserved; keep any future marketplace name ASCII and distinct. Here: .claude-plugin/marketplace.json name. [ref, security]
